prs.title: fix(browser): change default port to 23315
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- closes https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/9035

Browser mode's default port `63315` can be reserved by Windows when Hyper-V, WSL2, or Docker Desktop is running, for example [`63272-63371` on this issue](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/9035#issuecomment-4220359380). Binding a reserved port fails with `EACCES` ([voidzero-dev/vite-task#838](https://github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-task/pull/838), [facebook/lexical#8673](https://github.com/facebook/lexical/pull/8673)), but Vite only falls back to the next port on `EADDRINUSE` ([vite `http.ts`](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/v8.3.4/packages/vite/src/node/http.ts#L303-L312)), so the run fails. This PR changes the default to `23315`, chosen as described below.

## Port choice research

The new port, and the ports after it that additional browser projects take, stay clear of:

- Windows' dynamic port range, 49152-65535 by default ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/networking/default-dynamic-port-range-tcpip-chang)). Windows reserves blocks out of this range, and the blocks change on every reboot ([docker/for-win#3171](https://github.com/docker/for-win/issues/3171#issuecomment-853772306)). Machines where the range was changed to start lower can still hit a reserved block ([docker/for-win#3171](https://github.com/docker/for-win/issues/3171#issuecomment-554587817)), and `api: { port: 0 }` from #11641 covers them.
- Linux's default ephemeral range, 32768-60999 ([kernel

prs.title: feat(browser): mock modules through an import map
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
`vi.mock` registers an import map rule in the tester document that points the module URL at its mocked version (automock, the `__mocks__` file, or a factory shim whose export names are parsed from the original module), so providers never intercept requests and the HTTP cache stays on. The orchestrator probes whether the browser accepts an import map after a module has loaded; `browser.importMapMocks` forces it on or off. Firefox needs `dom.multiple_import_maps.enabled`; the Playwright provider sets it. A rejected mock registration now fails the import instead of being dropped.

Measured with https://github.com/ubugeeei-reproductions/js-test-runner-competition (Chromium, 9 workers, 500 files, 962 modules, 1,883 mocks per suite, wall time, median of 3 interleaved rounds):

| Suite | Vitest 5.0.3 | This change, `importMapMocks: false` | This change, default |
|---|---|---|---|
| nomock | 31.7 s | 29.9 s | 26.6 s |
| mock | 56.4 s | 57.7 s | 27.2 s |
| mixed | 44.0 s | 51.3 s | 27.1 s |

Known limits: `vi.unmock` and `vi.doUnmock` cannot remove a rule (this is already the case), a factory cannot add exports the original does not declare (similar to `viteModuleRunner: false`), and a module imported before `vi.mock` fails with an explicit error (which is a good thing).

Fixes https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11493
Fixes #8246

prs.title: feat: add `--last-failed` to run only failed tests
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Adds a CLI-only `--last-failed` flag that runs only the tests that failed in the last run.

- `results.json` stores the full names of failed tests per file (`failedTests`). A failure outside of tests (hook, collection) reruns the whole file.
- New `TestSpecification.testNames` filter. Names instead of ids, so adding or moving tests in the file keeps the selection.
- Works with `vitest list` and other filters. In watch mode, only the first run is narrowed.

prs.title: feat: support `Temporal.Instant` and `Temporal.ZonedDateTime` in `vi.setSystemTime()`
prs.author: Prajwal2246
prs.body:
_Updated description by @hi-ogawa_

- closes #8107

This PR adds support for `setSystemTime(Temporal.Instant | Temporal.ZonedDateTime)` by following Sinon’s structural `type TemporalTimelike = { epochMilliseconds: number }` shape to avoid requiring built-in Temporal types. The documented use cases are still only `Instant` and `ZonedDateTime`. `vi.useFakeTimers({ now })` already supported them through Sinon, so this PR adds tests and documents that existing behavior.

---

_Original description_

`vi.setSystemTime()` throws for a `Temporal.Instant` because `new Date(now)` invokes Temporal's throwing `valueOf`.

This PR accepts `Temporal.Instant` and `Temporal.ZonedDateTime` in `vi.setSystemTime()` and `vi.useFakeTimers({ now })` (ref #8107). `setSystemTime()` converts them with `epochMilliseconds`; fake-timers already accepts them for `now`.

The public types resolve Temporal constructors from `globalThis` and fall back to `never` when Temporal types are absent. A `ZonedDateTime` sets the instant, not the system time zone.

### Checks

- Temporal tests: 15 passed across threads, forks, and vmThreads.
- Adjacent date and mocked-time tests: 15 passed across the same pools.
- Changed files pass ESLint; `packages/vitest` builds.
- Package typecheck still reports three `CDPSession.send` errors in the untouched `src/node/pools/browser.ts`.

Disclosure per CONTRIBUTING.md: Claude assisted with the original change, and Codex assisted with this update.

prs.title: feat: introduce `--since-last-run` flag
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Closes #9917

This PR adds a new `--since-last-run` flag to run tests whose dependencies were changed since the last run. Unlike `--changed`, it doesn't require `git` and reuses a cached dependency tree instead of parsing every file on each invocation.

Additionally, this exposes a `resolver` object (that can return all dependencies) to custom vcs providers which is used by a new `mtime` provider. It is used by `--since-last-run` under the hood.

prs.title: fix(browser): advance fake timers in actions and expect.element
prs.author: julienw
prs.body:
### Description

Updated description by @hi-ogawa

- closes https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/10058

With fake timers enabled, a browser action such as `await locator.click()` times out when the element only appears after a timer such as `setTimeout` because nothing advances the fake clock while the action waits. `expect.element` has the same problem since Vitest 5, because it now uses `locator.findElement` in a retry loop that waits in real time, so `expect.poll` never gets to advance timers between attempts.

This PR fixes it by advancing fake timers while actions and element lookups wait, in the same spirit as `expect.poll`, `vi.waitFor` and `vi.waitUntil`. Locator actions work a bit differently from the others, because Vitest doesn't have access to the provider's actionability check loop. Instead, they advance fake timers by 50ms on a interval while the action runs (50ms is only heuristic value but taken from `poll/waitFor/waitUntil`'s default interval).

The following table is an overview of how the fake timer advance is wired up for each API in the Playwright provider:

| API | Advances fake timers | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Locator `click`, `dblClick`, `tripleClick`, `hover`, `unhover`, `clear`, `fill`, `selectOptions`, `upload`, `dropTo` | yes | `Action.#run` wraps the command with `advanceFakeTimersWhilePending`, which advances by 50ms every 50ms while it runs, even if the element already exists |
| `userEvent` counterparts of the above, `userEvent.dragA

prs.title: feat: support fake timers for `node:timers` and `node:timers/promise`
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
### Description

- closes https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/10871

There were multiple issues with previous code:
- `timersModule = __vitest_required__.timers` and `timersPromiseModule` were stashed during fake timer module scope but `__vitest_required__` wasn't setup yet at that point.
- `__vitest_required__.timers` is originally `import timers from "node:timers"` and this only patches esm-default and cjs exports objects. In order to propagate the mocking to named imports `import { setTimeout } from "node:timers"`, we can use node's `syncBuiltinESMExports` module util.

This PR fixes them and also guards node builtin mocking capability under new `useFakeTimers({ fakeNodeBuiltins: true })` option.

prs.title: fix: detect mock factory cycles that form later
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Follow-up to #11623.

A factory that imports a module which waits for the same factory gets the partial exports of that module. This check only ran when the import started. If the module was already evaluating but started to wait for the factory later (for example, a slow import before it), the factory and the module waited for each other until the test timed out.

The factory now also gets the partial exports when the module starts to wait while the factory waits for it.

This made `concurrent imports of an automocked module` and `factory gets partial exports of a module that waits for the mock` flaky on CI (for example in #11637). The new test cases fail every time without the fix.

prs.title: feat(browser): show trace steps timeline on terminal on test failure
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- closes https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11592

_TODO_
- (follow-up) unify types and utils with UI https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11604
- (follow-up) integrate with https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11492
- ~dump dom snapshot json file as attachment?~ (No, doesn't seem token efficient and aria snapshot is sufficient.)
- ~how to pick and match retry attempt and artifacts in reporter?~ deferred with https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11614
- ~tweak table format/column ordering?~

---

When a browser-mode test fails, the error shows what failed but not the steps that led there, which is often what you need for a flaky async test. The trace view records that sequence, but it's only visible in Vitest UI, the browser UI, and the HTML reporter.

This PR extends default reporter error output to include trace steps as a text table under. The timeline is rendered from the trace data the reporter already receives, so trace collection is unchanged.

_Example_

```
VITE_FAIL_TEST=1 pnpm --dir examples/lit test --run --browser.traceView --browser.headless
```

prs.title: fix: skip fs module cache for typed import.meta.glob
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
The cache bail-out checked for `import.meta.glob(`, so a call with a type argument (`import.meta.glob<T>(...)`) was cached with the glob already expanded. It now checks for `import.meta.glob`.

Fixes #11633

prs.title: fix: run tests that import a deleted file
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Fixes #11566

In SSR, Vite keeps an import it can't resolve in the module graph with the raw specifier as the id (or the aliased path with `noResolved` for an alias), so the walk dropped the link to the deleted file. A static import like that now marks the importer as failed, the same way the client environment already does. Dynamic imports are skipped because they can be caught, bare specifiers because Node can still load them.

prs.title: fix(browser): drop trace view warning without html reporter
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11594

`vitest run` with `--browser.traceView` and no HTML reporter used to warn that trace view is enabled without the HTML reporter, because the trace was only viewable there. Since #11594, the terminal prints the trace timeline under each failure, so this setup is useful on its own, including for CI logs and coding agents. This PR removes the warning. See https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11594 screenshot for how warning looked like.

prs.author: sheremet-va

prs.title: fix(browser): detect shared chunks via the optimizer
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Fixes #11652

The `no-cache` pin skipped shared optimizer chunks by matching `chunk-` in the URL. The Rolldown optimizer of Vite 8 names them `[name]-[hash].js`, and the esbuild optimizer also emits some chunks without the prefix. The check now uses `depsOptimizer.metadata.chunks`.

prs.title: fix(browser): clear screenshot stability timeout
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
`toMatchScreenshot` left its stability timer running after the screenshot won the race, so the process stayed alive until `timeout` elapsed. The timer is now cleared once the race settles.

Fixes #11656

prs.title: fix(ui): escape search text in explorer highlight
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
The explorer highlight built a regex from the raw search text, so a partial search like `nine (9` threw, and a search with balanced parentheses highlighted nothing. It also ran on the escaped name, so a search could match inside an HTML entity.

The highlight now escapes the search with `escapeRegExp`, splits the raw name, and escapes each part.

prs.title: fix(browser): measure prepare duration with one clock
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
The orchestrator now sends an absolute timestamp (`performance.timeOrigin + performance.now()`), and the tester measures the duration once at the end of `prepare()`.

Fixes #11651

prs.title: perf(expect): compare typed arrays in one loop
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Fixes #11657

Typed arrays are compared by index, and equal elements skip `equals`. Own non-index properties are still compared. A 2 MiB `toEqual` goes from ~1.5 s to ~125 ms locally.
